Consult Summary:
- Adult female with 7-day febrile illness (night sweats, myalgias, nausea) after recent travel to Vietnam; no localizing symptoms identified; urgent in-person assessment and blood tests planned to rule out malaria or other infection.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 7 days of fever with alternating hot/cold episodes, night sweats, generalized muscle aches, nausea with reduced appetite, fatigue; limited oral intake reported.
- Associated symptoms: Denies cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, dysuria, urinary frequency/urgency, rash, or new joint swelling/tenderness. Baseline headaches related to screen use; see conflict noted regarding migraines.
- Pertinent negatives: No recent respiratory or urinary symptoms; no rash; no neck stiffness.
- Travel: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; visited rural and urban areas; trekking/cycling. Took malaria prophylaxis daily and an additional unspecified tablet; names unknown.
- Past medical history: Chronic back pain (posture-related; in physiotherapy).
- Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at age ~68.
- Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine) — dose/route/frequency not documented. Over-the-counter ibuprofen and paracetamol at recommended doses; partial symptom relief.
- Allergies: Pollen allergy (hay fever). No medication allergies reported.
- Social history: Nurse; up to date on vaccinations including Hepatitis B. Non-smoker. Moderate alcohol intake. Performs moderate exercise a few times/week. Currently struggling at work due to fatigue.

Examination:

Impression:
- Acute febrile illness with night sweats, myalgias, and nausea without clear localizing source.
- Recent travel to Vietnam; malaria and other travel-related infections need to be ruled out.
- Possible dehydration risk given reduced oral intake.

Plan:
- Urgent in-person evaluation at central London clinic today for examination.
- Blood tests to be arranged following exam, including thick and thin blood films for malaria and inflammatory markers; urgency to be determined by in-person findings.
- Alternative option provided: attend local Emergency Department if clinic attendance is not feasible.
- Administrative: Clinician to message admin to book appointment; patient to call the provided number in the consultation notes to be scheduled.
- Work advice: Do not attend work until evaluation completed and cause identified.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals and physical examination.
  - Medication details (dose/route/frequency) for Seroxat and OTC use.
  - Detailed exposure history during travel (e.g., mosquito bites, freshwater exposure), pregnancy status, and comprehensive review of systems (respiratory, GI beyond diarrhea, etc.).
  - Drug allergy specifics beyond pollen.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Headaches/migraines: patient initially denied migraines (“No migraines”), later stated she sometimes struggles with migraines — conflict noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Minor disfluencies and a few incomplete phrases; overall intelligible with adequate clinical content.
